entries.title: Matthew 15:2
segments: Tradition; traditions were laws or precepts of men, which they said had been handed down by word of mouth from past generations, and many of which were afterwards written. They were often treated as of more authority than the laws of God. The scribes were the interpreters of these traditions, and could thus control the minds of the people. One of those traditions required the hands to be always washed before taking food. The object of this washing was to remove any ceremonial defilement that might have been unwittingly contracted in the intercourse of life. Our Saviour disregards it as a superstitious punctiliousness not required by the law of Moses. The Bible, as a rule of faith and practice, is perfect; and human traditions, however sanctioned, or by whomsoever taught, that add to it, take from it, or in any way pervert its meaning, are sources of error.

entries.title: Matthew 15:4
segments: A reception of the Bible as the word of God, and a familiar acquaintance with its contents, is a great safeguard against false doctrines and vicious practices. Hence, the good of men, as well as the glory of God, requires its universal circulation among all classes of people.

entries.title: Matthew 15:5
segments: It is a gift; that is, has been consecrated as a gift to the Lord. If children should announce to their parents that they had devoted to religious uses what might otherwise have been given to their support, the scribes said they were released from obligation to assist them, however much they might suffer. Thus, under pretext of religion, they nullified the law of God through their traditions.

entries.title: Matthew 15:6
segments: Honor not; namely, by providing for them a comfortable support.

entries.title: Matthew 15:8
segments: Draweth nigh; they pretended to honor God with words and outward observances, while their hearts and practices were opposed to him.

entries.title: Matthew 15:9
segments: For doctrines; teaching as the commands of God what were merely the commands of men.

entries.title: Matthew 15:11
segments: Not that; not food which goeth into the mouth, as the Pharisees pretended, but wickedness in the heart, coming out in false doctrines and wicked conduct, defileth a man.

entries.title: Matthew 15:13
segments: Every plant; he means false teachers, such as these Pharisees, with their corrupt doctrines and practices. Shall be rooted up; God is continually rooting them out of his earthly church, as he did the Pharisees of old, by his providence cooperating with his word and Spirit; and in the world to come the separation shall be final and perfect.

entries.title: Matthew 15:14
segments: Let them alone; regard not what they say, and have nothing to do with them.

entries.title: Matthew 15:15
segments: When we do not clearly understand the Scriptures, we should ask God to teach us. And though he may see that a right use of our faculties would have removed our ignorance, yet, if we sincerely desire to know the truth, he will, in the proper use of means, instruct us, and make us wise to salvation.

entries.title: Matthew 15:16
segments: Without understanding; common sense, if rightly exercised, would teach, that not food in the mouth, but sin in the heart defileth a man.

entries.title: Matthew 15:19
segments: The teaching of God will lead a man to place less reliance upon external observances, and to look more to the state of his heart, in obedience to the command of Christ, "Make the tree good," in order that the fruit may be good.

entries.title: Matthew 15:21
segments: Coasts of Tyre and Sidon; Zidonia, or Phoenicia, on the Mediterranean coast north of Palestine. Of this country Sidon was the earlier, and Tyre the later emporium.

entries.title: Matthew 15:22
segments: Woman of Canaan; for the Zidonians were descended from Canaan,
. By

, she is also called a Greek, as being a Gentile in her religion; and a Syrophoenician, as belonging to the Syrian Phoenicia, as distinguished from the Libyan Phoenicia of Africa. The Evangelists dwell on her gentile descent, because this was made prominent in our Lord's answer to her.

entries.title: Matthew 15:23
segments: Send her away; by granting her request.

entries.title: Matthew 15:24
segments: I am not sent; the reference of our Lord is here to his personal ministry. See note on chap

. In the Bible, and in the bestowment of his blessings in providence, God makes much of "due time." Men, even good men, are often in great haste. They would do things, if they could, much sooner than God does them; but they would not do them so well.

entries.title: Matthew 15:26
segments: Not meet; not suitable. Children's bread; that which was designed for the Jews, called children. Dogs; Gentiles, by the Jews called dogs. This he said to lead the woman to show her true character, which she soon did in a very striking manner.

entries.title: Matthew 15:27
segments: Eat of the crumbs; as dogs, without robbing the children, eat the crumbs which fall from the table, so she thought she might receive this mercy without injury to any one; and she had the fullest confidence in his power thus to help her.

entries.title: Matthew 15:28
segments: God often delays answering our requests, as a trail of our faith and humility. When these have been brought into exercise, a gracious answer will speedily come.

entries.title: Matthew 15:30
segments: Maimed; such as had lost a limb, a hand, or foot. Restoring them, therefore, was an act of creative power. There is nothing men need which Jesus Christ cannot bestow. All should therefore wait upon him; and if not weary in doing his will, in due time they shall receive all needed good.
